title: Premier League pushing for temporary concussion substitutes discussion at IFAB meeting
content:
Several organisations, including the Premier League, EFL, and FIFPRO, have increased the pressure on IFAB, football’s global lawmakers, to trial temporary concussion substitutes (TCSs).

The topic is not on the agenda for IFAB’s AGM, set to take place in Cardiff on Saturday, despite 30 leagues and unions writing to the body last month to formally request a trial.

They argue that TCSs are in the best interests of player welfare, allowing for longer medical examinations to take place in a quiet and controlled environment.

The Athletic reported last month that Premier League sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, believe there are currently no barriers to the trial’s introduction — given that a previous trial of introducing additional permanent concussion substitutes is now over.

Should TCSs not be discussed at IFAB’s AGM — there remains a possibility that the topic could be discussed in the “any other business” portion of the agenda — then Premier League sources have indicated that the league will seek an explanation from IFAB as to why the body has rejected its calls.

The league is also seeking clarity as to which factions within IFAB are against a trial of TCSs, as well as their rationale for that position.

A number of safeguards have been proposed to ensure that the introduction of TCSs would not be abused by teams for a tactical advantage — such as allowing the opposition to make their own additional substitution — and creating an oversight group to review video footage all instances where a TCS is used.

Should IFAB introduce a trial for TCSs, then the Premier League has indicated it would be committed to sharing data and learnings with FIFA and IFAB.

The Athletic has approached IFAB for comment.
